1970.notes: Laws of New York 1968, ch. 246 (HathiTrust uc1.b4378127, full view, seq 972-973) rewrote Tax Law s. 602 with a schedule for taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 1968: 2% of the first $1,000 rising by 1% per $2,000 bracket to 14% over $23,000 (each bracket's base amount checked against the rates). Laws 1970, ch. 1005 (uc1.b4378132, seq 1499-1503) raised the standard deduction and added s. 602(d), the 3% minimum tax, without changing the rates, and the 1977 act cited below lists ch. 246 of 1968 and ch. 1 of 1972 as the only earlier amendments of s. 602. ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1970-71 ed. (M-57), Table 36, rates as of December 31, 1970 (p. 79) prints the same 2%-14% schedule (14% over $23,000). The New York Department of Taxation and Finance's 1995 study 'Progressive Improvement' (Table 1) gives 15% over $25,000 for this year; the statute and ACIR show that bracket began with taxable years ending after December 31, 1971 (Laws 1972, ch. 1, as shown in the prior-law text of Laws 1977, ch. 70), so the study was not followed. No joint schedule: spouses were taxed separately on this schedule, as in this file's later entries. No deduction recorded, as in this file's other years (personal exemptions and an income-based standard deduction applied). Not modelled: the household credit, the minimum tax on tax preference items, and the no-tax threshold for low New York adjusted gross income.

1972.notes: Laws of New York 1977, ch. 70 (Sess. 200, v. 1; HathiTrust nyp.33433057658126, full view, seq 918-919), which shows the prior text of Tax Law s. 602 with its deletions in brackets: subsection (b), as amended by Laws 1972, ch. 1 and applying to taxable years ending after December 31, 1971, taxed 2% of the first $1,000 rising to 14% over $23,000 and 15% over $25,000 ($2,060 plus 15% of the excess); ch. 70 rewrote subsection (a) to apply that schedule to taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 1971 through those ending in 1977, and moved the 15% bracket to over $30,000 in (b) for taxable years ending after December 31, 1977. So 1972 has the 2%-15% schedule (15% over $25,000), the one ACIR prints for July 1, 1973 (this file's 1973 entry). Laws 1972, ch. 1 itself is in a search-only volume. No joint schedule: spouses were taxed separately on this schedule, as in this file's later entries. No deduction recorded, as in this file's other years (personal exemptions and an income-based standard deduction applied). Not modelled: the household credit, the minimum tax on tax preference items, and the no-tax threshold for low New York adjusted gross income. The 2.5% surcharge on tax for 1972 (DTF 'Progressive Improvement' study, Table 1 note b) is not modelled.

1973.notes: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1973-74 ed. (M-79), Table 141 (State Individual Income Taxes: Rates, July 1, 1973), Table 142 (personal exemptions) and Table 143 (standard deduction). Full statutory 2%-15% schedule as printed (identical to this file's 1976 entry). No joint schedule printed; as in this file's 1976 and 1978 entries, spouses were taxed separately on this schedule. No deduction recorded (as in the 1976 entry): Table 142 gives a $650 personal exemption ($1,300 married) and Table 143 a 15% standard deduction, max $2,000, with a low-income allowance. Not modelled: credit (full credit if tax is $100 or less, $200 minus tax if $100-$200); 6% minimum tax on NY minimum taxable income; no tax if NYAGI is $2,500 or less ($5,000 married, head of household or surviving spouse). The 2.5% surcharge was suspended for 1973 and 1974 (NY DTF 'Progressive Improvement' study, Table 1 note b; the ACIR table says it resumes 1/1/74).

1977.notes: Laws of New York 1977, ch. 70 (Sess. 200, v. 1; HathiTrust nyp.33433057658126, full view, seq 918-919), which shows the prior text of Tax Law s. 602 with its deletions in brackets: subsection (b), as amended by Laws 1972, ch. 1 and applying to taxable years ending after December 31, 1971, taxed 2% of the first $1,000 rising to 14% over $23,000 and 15% over $25,000 ($2,060 plus 15% of the excess); ch. 70 rewrote subsection (a) to apply that schedule to taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 1971 through those ending in 1977, and moved the 15% bracket to over $30,000 in (b) for taxable years ending after December 31, 1977. So calendar 1977 has the 2%-15% schedule (15% over $25,000), as in 1973-1976; the $30,000 top bracket of this file's 1978 entry starts with 1978 (a fiscal year spanning 1977 and 1978 prorates the two, s. 602(c)). No joint schedule: spouses were taxed separately on this schedule, as in this file's later entries. No deduction recorded, as in this file's other years (personal exemptions and an income-based standard deduction applied). Not modelled: the household credit, the minimum tax on tax preference items, and the no-tax threshold for low New York adjusted gross income. The 2.5% surcharge was repealed from 1977 (DTF study, Table 1 note b).

1978.notes: No joint schedule: spouses were taxed separately (combined return allowed), each on this schedule. Shown capped at the 12% maximum tax on personal service income (wages), per TSB-M-78(14)I; the statutory schedule continues 13% from $21,000, 14% from $23,000 and 15% over $30,000 for other income. Brackets below $11,000 (2%-7%) are those printed in TSB-M-87(10)I and match the $520 tax at $11,000 in TSB-M-85(9)I and the $1,780 tax at $23,000 in TSB-M-78(9)I. Personal exemption for 1978 not found; deduction left out. Standard deduction was 16% of NYAGI (min $1,400/$1,900, max $2,400); income-based, left out.
